t: 3485 – Longest Common Prefix of K Strings After Removal
o: After deleting words[i], we need the longest common prefix (LCP) of some k remaining strings. The LCP of a chosen set equals the depth of their deepest common trie node, so globally the answer is the deepest trie node with count ≥ k. Deleting words[i] only decrements counts along that word's root-to-leaf path; every other node is untouched. So per query: (a) the best depth among path nodes with original count ≥ k+1, and (b) the best depth among qualifying nodes OFF the path. For (b), precompute the few deepest 'maximal' qualifying nodes (cnt ≥ k, no qualifying child); they are mutually incomparable, so at most one lies on any root-to-leaf path — keeping the top 3 guarantees an off-path survivor. Example 1: "run"×3 and "jump"×2 with k=2 → removing a "jump" leaves three "run" (answer 3); removing a "run" leaves two "jump" (answer 4).
k: Model words as a trie; LCP of k strings = deepest node with cnt ≥ k.
Removal affects only nodes on the deleted word's path (cnt−1 there).
Maximal qualifying nodes are incomparable ⇒ at most one per path; keep top 3 by depth.

a.n: Approach 1: Trie Counts + Top-3 Maximal Nodes
a.i: Insert all words into a trie counting visits per node. Collect maximal nodes (cnt≥k, all children cnt<k), sort by depth descending, keep 3. Per query, walk the word's path recording the deepest node with cnt≥k+1 and the path node set; combine with the deepest kept maximal node not on the path.
s: Build trie with per-node counts and depths.
Find maximal qualifying nodes; keep top 3 by depth.
Per removal: walk the word, track best cnt≥k+1 depth and path set; answer = max of that and deepest off-path maximal node.
a.t: O(L + n) where L = total characters (≤1e5) — trie build, BFS, and per-word path walks are all linear in total length.

w: The incomparability argument (one maximal node per root-to-leaf path) is the crux — keeping just 2 suffices, 3 for safety. Pitfall: the n==k case returns all zeros; don't forget cnt≥k+1 (not k) along the deleted path. Follow-up: answer for inserting a word instead of deleting, or queries with varying k.
